title: Collapsing and expanding the left sidebar
current_note: Today a small chevron icon sits at the top right of the panel. It is easy to miss, and once the panel is collapsed there is nothing left to click.

variants.title: Floating pill on the divider
variants.rationale: The handle is about the boundary between panel and content, so it belongs on that boundary rather than inside one of the two. That also makes it independent of the panel's contents: it stays in the same place whatever is scrolled or selected, and it stays reachable when the panel is gone.
pros: Always in the same place, however wide the panel is
Reachable in both states without a second control
Reads as a divider affordance, which is what it is
cons: Overlaps the content in a very narrow window
Needs a shadow token to lift off both surfaces
A 22px target is small for touch

variants.title: The rail itself is the control
variants.rationale: If the collapsed state is already a visible strip, that strip can be the way back - then no extra control has to exist for it. The cost is that a surface has to advertise itself as clickable, which a strip of dots does not do on its own.
pros: No extra control to find; the largest possible target area
One fewer element in the expanded state
cons: Collapsing and expanding use different controls, which is asymmetric
A clickable surface without a label is easy to overlook
Blocks putting anything else clickable on the rail later

variants.title: The panel header is the control
variants.rationale: The header already exists, already carries the panel's name and already sits where you look when you deal with the panel. Making it the control means nothing new has to be found - and the name survives into the collapsed state instead of the panel becoming an anonymous strip.
pros: A labelled target instead of an icon that has to be guessed
Large target area in both states
The panel keeps its name when collapsed
cons: Rules out other click behaviour on the header later
Vertical text on the rail is harder to read
A whole row as a button can read as accidental
